title: Runtime budget silos with graceful model-variant degradation
creator: Priya Shah
description: Introduce per-tenant runtime budget "silohs" (short-lived budget windows) and a deterministic fallback ladder of model variants so that when a tenant's short-term spend risk or regional capacity pressure is detected, the router can degrade outputs in predictable steps instead of abruptly failing or overspending. Goals: (1) enforce soft and hard caps that limit cost exposure while preserving availability, (2) prefer cheaper GPU classes and preemptible capacity opportunistically without violating SLOs, and (3) provide clear telemetry and user-facing signals for degraded quality. This ticket implements the routing policy core + runtime hooks and a canary rollout plan for 5% of production tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Router can compute an active budget headroom value per-tenant per-minute and mark requests as normal / soft-degrade / hard-decline
Fallback ladder implemented: full model -> quantized variant -> shorter prompt window variant -> context-limited variant -> rate-limited decline
Routing prefers non-preemptible GPU only when predicted preemption risk exceeds configured threshold or SLO-critical requests
Metrics emitted: budget_burn_rate, degrade_rate_by_variant, eviction_probability_estimate, per-tenant-cost_delta
End-to-end test coverage for simulated spot-eviction bursts and scheduled budget exhaustion
Console shows per-tenant budget window and explains current degrade state (reason + expected time to recover)
